subject.title: Feature Request: Memory Trust Tagging by Source

question: Should OpenClaw establish a portable framework-owned provenance and influence contract enforced by the default memory path, or leave trust policy entirely to opt-in memory plugins and MCP integrations?
rationale: The choice changes OpenClaw's documented workspace-memory trust boundary, plugin SDK compatibility surface, stored data model, and default security posture; source inspection cannot determine that product and security intent.

options.title: Portable contract plus default enforcement
options.body: Add generic provenance, review, retention, and influence fields to the memory SDK and enforce a conservative reference policy in memory-core while allowing plugins to supply richer models.

options.title: Plugin-only trust policy
options.body: Keep core memory behavior unchanged and document external memory plugins or MCP integrations such as world-model-mcp as the supported path for trust-aware storage and retrieval.

options.title: Advisory guidance only
options.body: Retain the current Markdown guidance and untrusted prompt framing without persistent machine-enforced trust metadata.

recommendation.title: Portable contract plus default enforcement
recommendation.body: Add generic provenance, review, retention, and influence fields to the memory SDK and enforce a conservative reference policy in memory-core while allowing plugins to supply richer models.

likelyOwner.reason: This person supplied the prior design review and is connected by recent history to the central memory contracts and repository scope decisions.
